meaning.zh: 本課練習目標句型：Subject + will / may / should + verb + in due course。

rules.zh: 它不表示確實的日期或時間 In due course 表示事情會在適當時候發生，但沒有說明確實是哪一天或多久之後。 （有關決定將會在適當時候公布。） 這句沒有承諾公布日期。
rules.en: It does not give an exact date or time. In due course says that something will happen at the proper time, but not on which day or after how long. “The decision will be announced in due course” does not promise an announcement date.
examples: The decision will be announced in due course.

rules.zh: 它不等於 soon Soon 表示「很快」，但 in due course 不一定表示很快。 （文件很快便會歸還。） （文件會在完成正常程序後，於適當時候歸還。） 第二句沒有承諾事情會迅速完成。
rules.en: It does not mean soon. Soon means “in a short time”, whereas in due course does not necessarily promise speed. Compare: The documents will be returned soon. The documents will be returned in due course. The second sentence says that the documents will be returned at the proper stage after the normal process, without promising that this will happen quickly.
examples: The documents will be returned soon.
The documents will be returned in due course.

rules.zh: 它常用於正式或半正式場合 這個片語常見於： ● 商業電郵； ● 公司通知； ● 政府或學校公告； ● 顧客服務回覆； ● 行政和法律程序； ● 正式書面溝通。 在非常輕鬆的日常對話中，人們較常使用 later、when the time is right 或 when everything is ready。
rules.en: It is common in formal or semi-formal contexts, including business emails, company notices, government or school announcements, customer-service replies, administrative and legal procedures, and formal writing. In casual conversation, later, when the time is right, or when everything is ready is more common.

rules.zh: 它可以放在句末或句首 句末位置最常見： （你會在適當時候收到回覆。） 放在句首時，後面通常加逗號： （在適當時候，你會收到回覆。）
rules.en: It can come at the end or beginning of a sentence. The end position is most common: You will receive a reply in due course. At the beginning, it is normally followed by a comma: In due course, you will receive a reply.
examples: You will receive a reply in due course.
In due course, you will receive a reply.

rules.zh: 它不等於 in time In time 表示「及時、趕得及」，即在太遲之前完成。 （我們及時到達，趕上了會議。） In due course 表示「按照正常進度，在適當時候」。 （會議紀錄會在適當時候派發。）
rules.en: It does not mean in time. In time means early enough, before it is too late: We arrived in time for the meeting. In due course means at the proper time as the normal process continues: The meeting notes will be distributed in due course.
examples: We arrived in time for the meeting.
The meeting notes will be distributed in due course.

rules.zh: 它不等於 due date Due date 是截止日期。 （付款限期是星期五。） （付款會按正常程序在適當時候處理。）
rules.en: Do not confuse it with due date, which means a deadline. “The payment is due on Friday” gives the deadline; “The payment will be processed in due course” says it will be handled at the appropriate stage of the normal process.
examples: The payment is due on Friday.
The payment will be processed in due course.

rules.zh: 不要加入 the。正確：in due course。錯誤：in the due course。
rules.en: Do not add “the”. Correct: in due course. Incorrect: in the due course.

rules.zh: 如有明確限期，應直接說明日期 In due course 適合在確實時間尚未確定，或事情必須先經過正常程序時使用。 如對方需要知道明確期限，應直接說： （我們會在星期五前回覆。） 而不是只說： （我們會在適當時候回覆。）
rules.en: If there is a definite deadline, state the date directly. Use in due course when the exact time is not yet known or the matter must first go through the normal process. If the other person needs a clear deadline, say “We will reply by Friday” rather than only “We will reply in due course.”
examples: We will reply in due course.

benefits.zh: 這個句型能清楚表達事情不會立即發生，但會在完成必要程序後，於適當時候發生。
benefits.en: It clearly means “not now, but at the proper time” This structure tells the reader that something will happen later, after the necessary time or process.

benefits.zh: 你不需要生硬地叫對方等待，也可以禮貌地讓對方知道事情並未被忘記。 （請等待。我們現在不能回答你。） （你會在適當時候收到答覆。） 第二句較平和，也較適合正式溝通。
benefits.en: It gives polite reassurance. Instead of simply telling someone to wait, you can reassure them that the matter has not been forgotten. Compare: Please wait. We cannot answer you now. You will receive an answer in due course. The second version is calmer and better suited to formal communication.

benefits.zh: 使用 soon 可能令人以為事情很快便會完成。使用 in due course 則不會作出不必要的快速承 諾。
benefits.en: It avoids making a false promise Using soon may make people expect a quick result. In due course does not promise that the action will happen immediately.

benefits.zh: 這個片語適合用於公告、報告、商業電郵及行政溝通，能令語氣保持正式和中立。
benefits.en: It is useful in formal writing. The phrase suits notices, reports, business emails and administrative communication, and helps maintain a formal, neutral tone.

benefits.zh: 你不需要每次都詳細解釋「完成正常程序後，事情便會在適當時候發生」，可以用 in due course 簡潔地表達相同概念。 第二句更加簡潔，但仍保留「按正常程序在適當時候處理」的意思。
benefits.en: It can shorten a longer explanation. Instead of repeatedly explaining that something will happen after the normal steps have been completed, you can use in due course. Compare: We will contact you later, after the usual procedures have been completed and when the time is appropriate. We will contact you in due course. The second sentence is more concise while preserving the idea that the matter will be handled at the proper time through the normal process.
